articles.title: Iran faces a ‘silent economic war’, says Iranian president
Iran says held talks with Qatari mediators, urges US to accept conditions
articles.summary: Iran's foreign minister says reopening the strait is 'not difficult' if the US accepts reasonable conditions
articles.body: Iran says Qatari mediators have travelled to Tehran as the country’s foreign minister urges the United States to accept Iranian conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. News of the talks came as the commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) toured an underground missile facility on Saturday and the country’s president said Iran is facing a “silent economic war”. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Friday night and held two hours of talks with Iranian officials, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said, according to Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency. “We are in contact with mediators, including the Qataris, both in person and virtually, and are holding the necessary discussions to see whether another opportunity can be given to diplomacy,” he said on Saturday. The US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to launch strikes against Israel and Gulf states hosting US military bases. ⁠The conflict has drawn in countries across the region, disrupted shipping and ⁠pushed up global energy prices. Gharibabadi said the talks have not yet become formal negotiations. If they do, the technical details of Iran’s nuclear programme would be discussed, he added, but Iran’s position is that its enriched uranium must not leave the country. He also said Iran regards the US economic blockade as an act of war and will “take any action necessary” to break it. For his part, US President Donald Trump told Fox News on Saturday that he wants a “permanent” deal that stops Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. He said Iranian officials are “very, very difficult”. “We make a deal, and then they break the deal the next day,” he added. The ongoing talks in the region “must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally,” Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday, according to state television. “Our position is clear: as long as Iran’s demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” he said. “At the same time, we have always affirmed our readiness for dialogue, just as we are ready to defend ourselves.” Iran’s conditions have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Araghchi also said reopening the strait is “not difficult”, and requires the US only to “accept reasonable conditions that are in accordance with international law”, Tasnim reported. The minister said there is “no solution” unless Washington acknowledges its mistakes and fulfils its previous commitments. Iran has restricted shipping through the strait, which normally carried about a fifth of the world’s oil, since the war began. The US has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in response. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Saturday that his country is facing a “silent economic war” that is “tougher than a war with missiles”, according to the state news agency IRNA. Pezeshkian told a meeting of investors and producers that “a group of bullies, oppressors, and coercers sought to bring down our country”, but that Iranian businesses had managed market conditions well. Meanwhile, IRGC commander Major-General Ahmad Vahidi toured an underground missile facility, accompanied by Brigadier General Majid Mousavi, who heads the IRGC Aerospace Force, Tasnim reported. Vahidi was briefed on the force’s readiness and recent developments in its missile programme. The visit follows the Aerospace Force’s unveiling of a new underground facility earlier this month, where it displayed ballistic and cruise missiles and their launchers, Tasnim said.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz: Athlete swims through war zone to expose war's environmental toll
articles.summary: The following day, he witnessed another vessel engulfed in flames as he continued his swim through the strategic waterway
articles.body: Wearing nothing but swimming trunks, goggles and a UN-branded cap, 56-year-old ocean campaigner Lewis Pugh entered the waters off Oman’s Musandam Peninsula , where he found himself swimming within sight of burning ships and towering plumes of smoke . Just 20 minutes into his first swim, two explosions rocked the area and an oil tanker caught fire around four kilometres away, forcing him to abandon the attempt temporarily. The following day, he witnessed another vessel engulfed in flames as he continued his swim through the strategic waterway. A United Nations Patron of the Oceans, Pugh warned that pollution from damaged tankers could devastate coral reefs, mangroves and coastal ecosystems for decades. Yet sightings of dolphins, turtles and ospreys reminded him of the extraordinary wildlife at risk. Having previously swum in the Arctic, Antarctic and Red Sea to raise awareness of ocean conservation, he delivered a stark appeal: “We’ve got to stop the war. We’ve got to open the strait, and we’ve got to clean up this mess.”

Four soldiers, seven gunmen killed during drug cartel leader's arrest in Mexico
articles.summary: Four Mexican soldiers were killed in the armed confrontation in the municipality of Guasave
articles.body: Four Mexican soldiers and seven gunmen were killed during an operation to arrest Fausto Isidoro, leader of the Beltran Leyva criminal organization, in Mexico's Sinaloa state, APA reports, citing the country's Ministry of National Defense. According to the ministry, armed members of the criminal group resisted military personnel attempting to arrest the cartel leader, known as "Chapo Isidro." Four Mexican soldiers were killed in the armed confrontation in the municipality of Guasave. Seven gunmen were killed in return fire, while eight suspects were detained. Among those arrested were the group's leader Fausto Isidoro, his cousin and deputy Herman, known as "Serafin," and Jose, who was responsible for the organization's financial affairs. They were transported by military aircraft to Mexico City and handed over to the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Organized Crime. The other five suspects were transferred to the prosecutor's office in Culiacan, Sinaloa state. During the operation, authorities seized a large-caliber Barrett rifle, 10 firearms of various calibers, a grenade launcher, two hand grenades, ammunition, tactical equipment, narcotics and cash. According to Mexico's Ministry of National Defense, no civilians were injured during the operation.

Military analyst Phillips O'Brien on Ukraine and Europe being left out of Trump's talks
articles.summary: As President Trump met with Russian and Chinese counterparts, Ukraine and its European allies were left out of the talks
articles.body: As President Trump met with Russian and Chinese counterparts, Ukraine and its European allies were left out of the talks. NPR's Scott Simon talks with Phillips O'Brien of St. Andrew's University. SCOTT SIMON, HOST: Two summits this week on two sides of the world. President Trump was in China with leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, as European leaders gathered in Berlin with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to show their support for Ukraine. We're joined now by Phillips O'Brien, professor of strategic studies at University of St. Andrews in Scotland. Professor, thanks for being back with us. PHILLIPS O'BRIEN: I'm (ph) glad to be here. SIMON: What do you think we learned from the two summits this week? O'BRIEN: Well, we've learned that the United States is now officially much closer to Russia than it is to Ukraine or its European partners and that the United States' goal is to now bully Ukraine into giving up territory and people to Russia so that Putin gets a very good deal. The other thing we've learned is that Ukraine's support now is going to come from Europe and Europe alone, that the United States - oh, and Canada. But that, you know, it is up to Europe now to work with Ukraine to fight Russia off. And that's the reality. It's been the reality for a while, but that's what we actually had confirmed this week. And that was a useful thing. SIMON: Is Europe up to it? O'BRIEN: It is, certainly. I mean, Europe is - you would say, if you stepped back, Europe's more than capable of helping Ukraine. It has the money. It has the technology. It has the people. It has the brainpower. It has the engineering. What it doesn't have is the ability to think strategically on its own. It's become, in some ways, infantilized by the United States over the past 80 years. The United States did so much of its strategic thinking. And Europeans are panicked, really, when faced with the reality of having to do it without the USA. They are slowly adjusting, but the real issue's not material. It's mental. SIMON: Ukraine carried out a major attack this week on Russia. They hit a bridge linking Russia with the occupied Crimea Peninsula. And Russia retaliated with deadly missile strikes in Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown yesterday. What does this tell us about the military capabilities of both countries? O'BRIEN: Well, what we know - Russia's plan is to try and break Ukrainian civilian will this winter by committing war crimes on a daily basis. And that's been the - what they've been doing for a while. So they're going to try to kill civilians. They're trying to freeze civilians. They're trying to cut power. They are going to try and make Ukraine as unlivable as possible. And they have been helped a great deal by the United States because the United States has deprived Ukraine of air defense. And right now, by the way, the United States and - through Starlink and Starshield is actually hampering Ukraine's ability to defend itself by shooting down drones. So the Russian strategy's quite straightforward in - when we see it in action. What the Ukrainians are trying to do is, in some ways, something far more ambitious and actually, by the way, legal. And that is they're trying to cut the flow of supplies to occupied western Ukraine. It's very hard for the Russians to get supplies into Crimea and then occupied parts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia. And so what the Ukrainians seem to be trying to do is to isolate those regions and make it very difficult for the Russians to supply them. SIMON: The U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said he believes that Russia - his phrase was comfortable - is comfortable with... O'BRIEN: (Laughter). SIMON: ...NATO-like - well, you anticipate the question... O'BRIEN: (Laughter). SIMON: ...NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine... O'BRIEN: Yeah. SIMON: ...As a way to end the war. Does this strike you as a plausible proposal for negotiations? O'BRIEN: Well, there's two things to say. NATO-like is nothing. Yeah, there's either NATO or not NATO. And, you know, NATO-like can be whatever they want it to be. But the key thing is Kushner's desperate to get a deal because they understand what's coming down the pike with the new Congress. And by the way, this was - they're saying it, oddly, to the Ukrainians and Europeans, who are then reporting it to the press, that what's going on is they - that, you know, Kushner and Witkoff and the Americans are saying, we need a deal by January 3 because we're going to have less power when the Democrats take over Congress. But this is simply posing. It's arguments, you know, that Putin is not going to accept anything like a real security guarantee for Ukraine. But it's the Trump administration's desperation to get something for Putin before the Democrats take over Congress. SIMON: It's been almost five years since Russia launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. It's a long time for Ukraine to hold out, isn't it? What's your sense of where the war might be heading? O'BRIEN: Well, it certainly is a long time, and they've done a remarkable job. And from the Ukrainian perspective, when you talk to them, their view is, we have no option. I mean, if we're - if we so - don't hold out, we'll be dead. I mean, it's quite clear that the Russians don't care about their lives, don't care about their cultures or societies. So resisting isn't really an option to them. They have to resist, or they will be wiped out. The thing that is very frustrating, and I got this from when I was last in Ukraine and talking to them, is they feel, in many ways, the war is heading in their favor. They're more adaptable. They're doing better on the front line. They were doing a very successful strike campaign against Russian oil refineries and logistics. But then the United States has, you know, come out and switched sides. And so the United States is providing a huge lifeline to Putin, which is really helping the Russians by leaving Ukrainian cities defenseless. And that's the reality of that - what they face. SIMON: Phillips O'Brien, professor at University of St. Andrews in Scotland. Thank you so much for being with us. O'BRIEN: Thank you. Copyright © 2026 NPR. All rights reserved. articles.title: Sara’s father shared photographs of his daughter’s attack
articles.summary: Sara’s father at today’s protest in Ohrid showed photographs of his beaten daughter with bruises on her face
articles.body: Sara’s father at today’s protest in Ohrid showed photographs of his beaten daughter with bruises on her face. With a photograph of his 26-year-old daughter Sara Gjorgjieska, on which the injuries and bruises on her face are visible, Ljupco Gjorgjieski today joined the protest against violence against attacks on women and femicide in Ohrid. His daughter was brutally beaten on 15 November, according to the indictment, by her boyfriend Kristijan Koraboski, after which she was left unconscious on the street. “This is my daughter Sara. May no parent see their child like this and experience what happened to us,” Gjorgjieski stated, showing the photograph of the injured Sara.

articles.title: Previously rejected Uzbek family ends 2-year church sanctuary after new asylum bid
articles.summary: According to the organization, church asylum coordinator Herman Stomphorst said Asylum Seekers (COA) is arranging accommodation for them
articles.body: The Uzbek Babayants family will leave the Open Hof church in Kampen within a few days, where they have received church sanctuary for the past two years. According to the organization, church asylum coordinator Herman Stomphorst said Asylum Seekers (COA) is arranging accommodation for them. “Until then, they may stay here in the church,” Stomphorst said shortly before the continuous church service ended on Saturday afternoon. The family of four children has lived in the Netherlands since 2014. Because they have now submitted a new residence application, the family may legally remain in the Netherlands for the duration of the procedure. The family itself chose to leave the church, supported by a ruling from the Council of State. In July, the Council of State ruled that three asylum-seeker families with children who have lived in the Netherlands for years and built lives here may stay. The highest administrative court determined that the minister must give greater weight to the interests of the children. For Stomphorst, Saturday is a tense day. “I worry that the procedure will take a very long time,” he said. “But I am reassured because the Council of State has been very clear.” At the same time, he is prepared for the possibility that things may not turn out well. “We are not naive. There is certainly a chance that the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) will reject the application again. The Babayants family only submitted a new application this week, according to the family’s lawyer, Inge Zuidhoek, because it had to be properly prepared. Additional information was included about the family and their roots in the Netherlands. Zuidhoek hopes this new information will lead to a fresh assessment by the IND. “If it had no chance of success, I would not have submitted a new application,” she said.

articles.title: Suffolk village votes to ‘leave the UK’ over plans to house asylum seekers nearby
articles.summary: Approximately 500 people in Barnham were eligible to take part in the symbolic vote on Saturday
articles.body: Residents of a Suffolk village have voted to “leave the UK” in a referendum held in response to government plans to house 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former military base. Approximately 500 people in Barnham were eligible to take part in the symbolic vote on Saturday. There were 257 votes for independence, 16 against and one spoiled ballot. After the vote, Helen Beck, the chair of Barnham Residents’ Association, said Barnham’s flag would be a stone-curlew on a “Suffolk blue background”. RAF Barnham was one of three Ministry of Defence sites named in June by the government as potential locations for new developments to house asylum seekers. A similar referendum was held in Piddington, Oxfordshire in September, with residents also voting to leave the UK amid plans to house more than 1,000 migrants at another former military base. In Barnham, the plans have prompted protests outside the site. The referendum asked residents whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status”, which is a similar system to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. John Bauer, the parish council chair, said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” but remove itself from Home Office jurisdiction. While in opposition the Labour party had attacked the Conservative policy to house asylum seekers on military bases; once in government, however, the party backtracked. The Conservatives have also reversed their position, with Kemi Badenoch telling frustrated villagers “the Conservative party is on your side”. “We know that the problem of the boats needs to stop and we have got a plan to stop it,” she said on Friday. Earlier this month, it was announced construction company Kier would design the new camp at RAF Barnham. Before Saturday’s vote Labour’s Dr Peter Prinsley, the local MP, said he was against the development of the site. Prinsley said the plans resembled a “concentration camp”, and warned that planning permission may be difficult to attain due to environmental concerns about rare species living in the area – in particular, stone-curlews – with previous development applications nearby having been turned down. “This is a symbolic referendum,” Prinsley said. “It’s not going to produce a binding result. I’m expecting that [the result] will be hugely in favour of becoming a crown dependency. There are 500 electors, so I’m expecting it to be 500 – nil.” He added that the government “is doing an awful lot to deal with the irregular migration problem”, and highlighted that net migration may come down to “more or less zero by the end of the year”. But he added that he didn’t think “the large army camps in remote locations are ever likely to be appropriate for the distribution of people seeking asylum. The fact is that people who arrive here on small boats are not illegal migrants. They are people who are seeking asylum. Our political opponents have described these people as ‘illegals, criminals, rapists’, and all sorts of things that they’re not. They’re just people who have arrived on small boats. The government is getting a grip on this problem, but it’s a complicated problem.” He said the proposed Barnham site had particular issues which may make it unsuitable. “It’s a remote location without any pedestrian access, it’s on a very hazardous main road. When it was used as military accommodation there were serious accidents on that road. “It’s also a site of special scientific interest because it is the nesting site for stone-curlews, which will make any planning application very difficult – even a government planning application – because these are worldwide protections.” He suggested “disused office blocks in some of the larger cities” may be more appropriate places to house asylum seekers, with more local services available. “It feels like a concentration camp,” Prinsley added. “It doesn’t feel like a place that has a compassionate approach to people who are fleeing persecution and are being processed for asylum.” He also said legitimate criticism of the plans had been co-opted by opposition parties who are aiming to “stir up racial discord”. A Home Office spokesperson said: “We recognise the strength of feeling in local communities and are listening carefully to the concerns being raised. “The government is working on a fairer distribution of asylum accommodation across the country, with over £1bn saved in costs since the election. “This includes closing all asylum hotels and moving to alternative accommodation, including former military sites. These are designed to be self-contained, with 24/7 security and CCTV, to reduce the impact on local communities.”

Dodik: SNSD Candidate will be the prime-designate for forming the new RS Government
articles.summary: However, he declined to reveal the name, noting that it would be announced by the President of Republika Srpska
articles.body: Milorad Dodik, President of the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD), stated today that the party’s candidate will be the Prime Minister-designate for the new Government of Republika Srpska. However, he declined to reveal the name, noting that it would be announced by the President of Republika Srpska. “As the strongest political organization in Republika Srpska, we have a candidate for Prime Minister-designate, but we will not disclose the name. We leave it to the President of Republika Srpska to make that announcement. I can only say that it is not me,” Dodik said at a press conference following a meeting of the SNSD Presidency in Banja Luka. Dodik also stated that the SNSD is clearly defining the policies to be implemented by the new government, emphasizing that the party assumes a special responsibility for their execution. “Our goals are a peaceful and stable Republika Srpska, an improvement in the material well-being of the people, and maximum engagement from the Government of Republika Srpska. We want to translate this major victory into significant stability and tangible benefits for the citizens,” said Dodik, announcing the continuation of activities with coalition partners. Regarding the election of delegates to the House of Peoples of the Parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dodik stated that the SNSD will nominate four candidates, and that the list of candidates for the Council of Peoples of Republika Srpska has also been finalized. “A certain number of votes remained unallocated in terms of support for a fifth candidate for the House of Peoples,” Dodik added, without mentioning any specific names. It was previously announced that the SNSD’s nominees for delegates to the House of Peoples of BiH are Sredoje Nović, Dušica Šolaja, Nikola Dronjak, and Radovan Kovačević. Commenting on the decision by the Constitutional Court of BiH, which declared the provision of the Criminal Code of Republika Srpska – regarding the penalization of displaying symbols of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina (ARBiH) – to be unconstitutional, Dodik stated that the SNSD would not accept this ruling. He announced that no minister from Republika Srpska in the Council of Ministers of BiH would vote for any decision until, as he put it, this ruling is withdrawn. Željka Cvijanović, a member of the Presidency of BiH and the SNSD Presidency, assessed that the Constitutional Court’s decision amounts to political maneuvering and serves to undermine the constitutional order of BiH, Fena writes.

Vance stops short of endorsing Trump’s claim that Iran was close to nuclear weapon
articles.summary: I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” Trump said
articles.body: At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that it was essential for the US to go to war with the Islamic republic. In the White House briefing room, Trump was asked about reporting this week that he was unhappy with the US vice-president’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war. “I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” Trump said. “I thought the statement was fine, except I would have had one other thing, that if it were asked, I would have said that: ‘Would you do it again?’ And absolutely, the answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon.” However, Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to developing a nuclear weapon this year that it was necessary to go to war, which he has made dozens of times in the past nine months, is undermined by public evidence and contradicts his own previous statements on US strikes against Iranian facilities in 2025. At a campaign rally in Alaska last month, Trump insisted that he had to join Israel in attacking Iran in February because, “they were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon”. That claim appears at odds with what his then director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, testified to Congress on 25 March 2025, two months into Trump’s second term: that US intelligence agencies reported that Iran had not tried to make a nuclear weapon for more than two decades. The US intelligence community, Gabbard said, “continues to assess Iran is not building a nuclear weapon and supreme leader Khamenei has not authorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003”. Despite that assessment, three months later, on 21 June 2025, Trump ordered the US bombing of Iran’s nuclear enrichment facilities. The strikes, Trump told the public that night , “were a spectacular military success. Iran’s key nuclear enrichment facilities have been completely and totally obliterated.” Eight months after that, however, when Trump announced the start of a full-scale war on Iran early on 28 February 2026, he said in a video statement from Mar-a-Lago the war was necessary to “ensure that Iran does not obtain a nuclear weapon”. The morning after this month’s midterm elections, Vance said in a statement posted on social media: “The reason we lost is the war.” “If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so,” he added. “Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost.” In the White House briefing room on Friday, after Trump said that Vance should have said the war was necessary, a reporter asked the vice-president whether he would argue that the war in Iran was worth it. In his response, Vance said it was not his place to second-guess the president, but refrained from actually endorsing Trump’s claim that the war was essential to stop Iran from creating a nuclear weapon. “Look, what I’ve said is the goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we need to be doing. It’s the biggest state sponsor of terrorism. If they had a nuclear weapon, they would use it as leverage or, God forbid, they would attack and kill thousands, hundreds of thousands, of innocent people,” Vance said. “I think the president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again.” “My view is that my goal is, and my job is, to support the president of the United States,” the vice-president said. The vice president’s office did not respond to a request to comment.

articles.title: Melania Trump says another ceasefire in Ukraine could happen 'before Christmas'
articles.summary: Melania Trump has suggested a new localised ceasefire in Ukraine could be agreed in the coming weeks
articles.body:
Melania Trump has suggested a new localised ceasefire in Ukraine could be agreed in the coming weeks.

Donald Trump's wife brokered the six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky last month, when a humanitarian operation saw hundreds of citizens evacuated to Ukrainian-held territory.

She later brought Ukrainian and Russian officials together at the White House to mark the truce.

Asked on a Fox News special programme about her wishes for Christmas, the first lady said: "Well, it's world peace, of course, but first of all, I really would like to have more ceasefires.

"We could do it very fast if both Ukraine and Russia are willing. I am in talks already.

"So maybe we will have another ceasefire before Christmas."

In a social media post last week, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv has proposed 10 more areas in the Russian-controlled parts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia where "a similar humanitarian operation" to Oleshky was needed.

articles.title: Drones attack cargo ship close to Russian border, Moscow says
articles.body:
A cargo ​vessel ‌heading to the Kaliningrad exclave was ​attacked by two drones in ⁠the Gulf of Finland, ‌a Russian official has said.

The governor of the Leningrad region, Aleksandr Drozdenko, said the vessel was struck by the drones in neutral waters, but was only three nautical miles from ‌Russia's border.

The ship's crew was evacuated ⁠after the incident.

The Finnish Border Guard, which shared an image of the vessel on fire, said it was preparing for "potential environmental damage" as it led the rescue operation.

Following the strike, the ship has drifted from international waters into Finnish territorial waters, it added.

The Gulf of Finland and Kaliningrad are Russia's only access points to the Baltic Sea, and have been regular targets for Ukrainian attacks.

St Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, sits on the gulf's coast.

articles.title: Seven-year-old boy and paramedic killed in Russian strike on Zelenskyy's hometown
articles.summary: Two people have been killed in Russian ballistic missile strikes on the city of Kryvyi Rih overnight
articles.body:
Two people have been killed in Russian ballistic missile strikes on the city of Kryvyi Rih overnight.

Ukrainian broadcaster Suspilne reported the victims were a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old ambulance paramedic who arrived at the scene of the attack.

A further 60 people were injured in the attacks with around half hospitalised, as apartment buildings, a restaurant and a hospital were damaged in the city.

Russia's defence ministry said it struck a thermal power ​plant ⁠in the city.

Kryvyi Rih, in the Dnipropetrovsk region, is Volodymyr Zelenskyy's home town.

editorialRejections.body: According to Ukrinform, the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine reported this and released a video. “The target was hit using an automated system. The servicemen’s high level of training, professional command of modern technologies and coordinated teamwork enabled them to successfully engage the aerial target,” the State Border Guard Service said. The Filin missile belongs to the class of small, long-range surface-to-surface missiles. It is approximately 3.5 meters long. editorialRejections.title: Melania Trump hopes for new ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia by Christmas
editorialRejections.summary: She made the remarks during the National Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony, broadcast on Fox News , Ukrinform reports
editorialRejections.reason: Ukraine coverage requires an international news source
editorialRejections.body: She made the remarks during the National Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony, broadcast on Fox News , Ukrinform reports. When asked about her Christmas wish, Melania Trump said that she wished for peace around the world, but above all hoped to see more ceasefires. She expressed confidence that this could be achieved quickly if both Ukraine and Russia were willing, adding that she was already holding talks with representatives of both countries and hoped another ceasefire could be reached by Christmas. Melania Trump also referred to the ceasefire agreement that had enabled a humanitarian mission in Oleshky, noting that she had been involved in every detail of the process and was pleased that 800 people had been released. She added that they now had access to warm shelter, food and medicine, noting that many of those rescued were elderly people and children. She expressed hope that they would have a good Christmas. As Ukrinform previously reported, President Volodymyr Zelensky named settlements in the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions where Ukraine proposes conducting humanitarian missions following the successful evacuation of civilians from Oleshky. A ceasefire was in effect in the area around the temporarily occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region from October 27 to November 1 to facilitate a humanitarian operation.

editorialRejections.title: Injury toll in Russian attack on Kryvyi Rih rises to 73, including nine children
editorialRejections.summary: Oleksandr Vilkul, Head of the Kryvyi Rih Defense Council, reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform
editorialRejections.reason: Ukraine coverage requires an international news source
editorialRejections.body: Oleksandr Vilkul, Head of the Kryvyi Rih Defense Council, reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform. Vilkul noted that efforts to deal with the aftermath of the ballistic missile and drone attacks carried out by Russian forces yesterday evening and overnight are still underway in the city. “Two people were killed: a 20-year-old emergency medical technician and a seven-year-old boy... The number of injured has risen to 73, including nine children, three emergency medical workers and employees of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine who were helping people,” Vilkul said. He specified that 29 injured people, including six children, are being treated in hospitals. The youngest victim is just three years old. “Nine are in serious condition, including two children. Doctors are doing everything necessary to save their lives,” Vilkul stressed. According to him, the Russian strikes damaged around 26 apartment buildings, a hospital, educational institutions, an enterprise, business facilities, a restaurant, garages, ambulances and vehicles. Municipal workers, power engineers, heating and gas utility crews have been working to deal with the aftermath of the attack since Friday evening. The gas supply situation has now been stabilized, electric public transport has resumed after trolleybus power lines were severed, and significant progress has been made in restoring water supplies. However, “there is still a lot of work to do,” the head of the city’s Defense Council stressed. As Ukrinform previously reported, Russian forces attacked Kryvyi Rih with two ballistic missiles and then launched a follow-up attack with jet-powered drones.

editorialRejections.title: Ukraine, UK agree to jointly produce Ukrainian middle- and deep-strike drones in Britain
editorialRejections.summary: We are launching projects that strengthen the capabilities of both our countries and accelerate the development of our defense industries
editorialRejections.reason: Ukraine coverage requires an international news source
editorialRejections.body: The ministry noted that Ukrainian drones that have already proven their effectiveness will be manufactured with funding from the United Kingdom, and the output of the joint production facilities will be allocated to meet the needs of the Ukrainian military. “We are launching projects that strengthen the capabilities of both our countries and accelerate the development of our defense industries. Ukraine has effective defense solutions and invaluable experience in fighting the enemy. We are combining these with the United Kingdom’s manufacturing capabilities to scale up proven systems for our Defense Forces more quickly. The resilience of our partnership, its quality and its ability to deliver results in the long term are important to us,” Khmara said. During the meeting, he thanked the United Kingdom for its leadership in supporting Ukraine and for the air defense assistance package announced at the Ramstein meeting. “The United Kingdom was among the first countries to promptly transfer LMM missiles to Ukraine from its own stockpiles in exchange for future deliveries. Yevhenii Khmara thanked the UK for this decision, as such systems are critically important for countering jet-powered Shahed drones,” the Ukrainian defense ministry noted. The two sides also focused on further steps to strengthen Ukraine’s air defenses, particularly accelerating additional deliveries of LMM missiles from existing stockpiles. In addition, they discussed strengthening Ukraine’s long-range strike capabilities and upgrading Ukrainian-made missiles. The Ministry of Defense reported that Khmara also took part in a meeting between the British delegation and President Volodymyr Zelensky, during which the sides discussed further support for Ukraine and the development of the Ukrainian-British defense partnership. As Ukrinform previously reported, Volodymyr Zelensky discussed with UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting specific defense capabilities that Ukraine needs right now.

editorialRejections.title: Apartment building 'destroyed' in Kyiv Oblast following Russian drone attack, at least 2 injured.
editorialRejections.summary: A fire broke out at the apartment amid the strike, leaving units on all five floors "destroyed," Tkachenko added
editorialRejections.reason: Ukraine coverage requires an international news source
editorialRejections.body: Russia launched yet another drone attack on Ukraine's national capital region overnight on Nov. 22, damaging an apartment building in Kyiv Oblast and injured at least two people, officials reported. Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv Oblast Military Administration, reported that a five-story residential building was damaged in the Vyshhorod district of Kyiv Oblast, just north of the capital, amid the attack. A fire broke out at the apartment amid the strike, leaving units on all five floors "destroyed," Tkachenko added. A 22-year-old woman and a child were injured in the attack. The full extent of the damage caused was not immediately clear. Over the past several months, Russia has intensified its drone and missile attacks against the Ukrainian capital ahead of the upcoming winter months. In Moscow's most recent large-scale attack on Kyiv on Nov. 20, Russia damaged a critical infrastructure facility as well as several bridges in the city. At least nine people were killed and 30 other injured in the attack. Amid the increase in attacks, President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly called on Ukraine's allies to accelerate promised air defense deliveries, particularly U.S.-made PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptor missiles for Patriot systems.

editorialRejections.title: Russia, Georgia agree upon measures to expand trade
editorialRejections.summary: The significant potential for expanding practical cooperation in spheres of mutual interest was noted at the meeting, the deputy minister said
editorialRejections.reason: Local outlet reports an event outside its home country without a local subject
editorialRejections.body: MOSCOW, November 22. /TASS/. Russia and Georgia have agreed upon a number of measures to expand bilateral trade, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin told TASS, commenting on the results of the meeting with Special Envoy of the Georgian Prime Minister for Relations with Russia George Zurabashvili in Minsk. The significant potential for expanding practical cooperation in spheres of mutual interest was noted at the meeting, the deputy minister said. "The Russian side informed about measures taken, called to facilitate further increase in supplies of Georgian agricultural and winemaking products to the capacious market of our country. The issue of additional authorizations for motor vehicle transportation was agreed in the initiative of the Georgian side," Galuzin noted. The Russian side is satisfied with the outcome of talks, the deputy foreign minister said. "The participants hailed the steady positive dynamics of the trade turnover and the tourist flow, which act as the powerhouse of bilateral relations," he added.

editorialRejections.title: Russia, Georgia to maintain regular direct dialogue — Russian diplomat
editorialRejections.summary: It was agreed to set the direct Russian-Georgian dialogue in a new format on a regular basis
editorialRejections.reason: Local outlet reports an event outside its home country without a local subject
editorialRejections.body: MOSCOW, November 22. /TASS/. The direct dialogue between Russia and Georgia in a new format will become regular, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin told TASS, commenting on the results of the meeting with Special Envoy of the Georgian Prime Minister for Relations with Russia George Zurabashvili in Minsk. "It was agreed to set the direct Russian-Georgian dialogue in a new format on a regular basis. We once again express our gratitude to Belarusian friends for the high level of organization of the Russian-Georgian meeting," the deputy minister said. Moscow and Tbilisi are ready to the phased establishment of ties in certain spheres, Galuzin noted. "A number of current international issues was discussed in detail, and regional security problems proceeding from the principle of responsibility of South Caucasian countries and their direct neighbors for solving problems in the region. Both sides expressed readiness to the phased establishment of ties in the cultural-humanitarian sphere and strengthening of communications between the people," he said. The first talks between Galuzin and Zurabashvili were held on Thursday in Minsk.

editorialRejections.title: Mapped: The route of Sparta II before suspected drone strike
editorialRejections.summary: Data from MarineTraffic shows that the Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad had stopped in Finnish waters after 6am UTC
editorialRejections.body:
Data from MarineTraffic shows that the Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad had stopped in Finnish waters after 6am UTC.

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and by Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

While Ukraine has not taken responsibility for the strike, the Finnish authorities say it's likely to be behind it - that would make the first such strike in the Gulf of Finland from Kyiv during this war.

editorialRejections.title: Strike on Russian cargo ship in Gulf of Finland 'likely carried out by Ukraine'
editorialRejections.body:
We reported earlier on a Russian cargo ship catching fire in the Gulf of Finland after a reported drone attack (see 10:35 post).

The Finnish Border Guard, who are leading the response to the incident, have now identified the affected ship as the Sparta II, a Russian vessel sanctioned by the US.

The force said the Sparta II was known to have links to Russian armed forces and that it couldn't rule out military material being on board the vessel.

The Sparta II crew are being evacuated, the border guard added.

A spokesperson for Finland's defence force said the strike on the vessel was likely carried out by Ukraine.
editorialRejections.reason: Duplicate development; kept BBC

editorialRejections.title: Russia responds with its own cargo ship attack in Black Sea
editorialRejections.summary: Russia has carried out a drone attack on a Ukrainian vessel in the Black Sea, the country's defence ministry has said
editorialRejections.body:
Russia has carried out a drone attack on a Ukrainian vessel in the Black Sea, the country's defence ministry has said.

It said a dry cargo ship was struck earlier today while delivering dual-use cargo to the Ukrainian armed forces.

The attack comes after a Russian cargo ship was left on fire after being hit by drones in the Gulf of Finland.
